title: A Noetherian local ring is regular iff its completion is
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local ring and $A^\wedge=\varprojlim_nA/\mathfrak m^n$ its $\mathfrak m$-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] (a Noetherian local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak mA^\wedge$). Then $A$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] if and only if $A^\wedge$ is a regular local ring.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07NY (lemma-completion-regular, line 10668) and its proof (Algebra Lemma 00OF flat-under-regular for the converse, More on Algebra Lemma 07NV completion-dimension)

proof.text: (Setup.) $A^\wedge$ is a Noetherian ring [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian] and a local ring whose maximal ideal is $\mathfrak m_{A^\wedge}=\mathfrak mA^\wedge$, the ideal generated by $\iota(\mathfrak m)$ for the canonical map $\iota:A\to A^\wedge$ [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring]; so it makes sense to ask whether $A^\wedge$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Moreover $\dim A^\wedge=\dim A$ [lem-weil-pbc-completion-dimension]; put $d=\dim A$, a finite number. Recall that by definition a Noetherian local ring $(R,\mathfrak m_R)$ is regular iff $\mathfrak m_R$ is generated by $\dim R$ elements [def-weil-regular-scheme]; equivalently, iff $\mathfrak m_R$ is generated by at most $\dim R$ elements (pad a shorter generating list with zeros).

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07NY (lemma-completion-regular): 'mA^ is the maximal ideal of A^', 'dim(A) = dim(A^) (Lemma 07NV)'

proof.text: ($A$ regular $\Rightarrow$ $A^\wedge$ regular.) Let $x_1,\dots,x_d$ generate $\mathfrak m$. Every $a\in\mathfrak m$ is $a=\sum_ir_ix_i$ with $r_i\in A$, so $\iota(a)=\sum_i\iota(r_i)\iota(x_i)$; hence the ideal $\mathfrak mA^\wedge$ generated by $\iota(\mathfrak m)$ is generated by $\iota(x_1),\dots,\iota(x_d)$. By step 1, $\mathfrak m_{A^\wedge}=\mathfrak mA^\wedge$ is thus generated by $d=\dim A^\wedge$ elements, so the Noetherian local ring $A^\wedge$ is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme].

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07NY, second part ('mA^ is the maximal ideal of A^ and hence m_{A^} is generated by at most dim(A^) elements. Thus A^ is regular'); Stacks phrases the count through dim m/m^2 = dim A, here the generators of m are used directly

proof.text: ($A^\wedge$ regular $\Rightarrow$ $A$ regular.) Write $\mu(I)$ for the minimal number of generators of an ideal $I$. If $A^\wedge$ is regular, $\mu(\mathfrak m_{A^\wedge})\le\dim A^\wedge=d$ [def-weil-regular-scheme] [lem-weil-pbc-completion-dimension]. Since $\mu(\mathfrak m)=\mu(\mathfrak m_{A^\wedge})$ [lem-weil-pbc-completion-maximal-ideal-generators] (which rests on $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2\cong\mathfrak mA^\wedge/(\mathfrak mA^\wedge)^2$, Algebra 05GG, and Nakayama, Algebra 00DV), $\mathfrak m$ is generated by at most $d=\dim A$ elements, so $A$ is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme]. (Stacks deduces this direction from Algebra Lemma 00OF, regularity descends along the flat local map $A\to A^\wedge$; the generator count is a shorter argument with the same ingredients as the forward direction, and avoids a new node for 00OF.)
